Simulate data from a fitted model

Source: R/fp_calibrate_fit.R
simulate.fp_occu.Rd

Generates new detections from an fp_occu fit, keeping everything else of the original data: the sites and their covariates, the automated occasions with their observation covariates and recorders, which sites and occasions were verified, and which occasions were checked under the observation-confirmation design. Only the latent occupancy states and the detections are drawn anew, from the fitted model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, truth = c("mean", "posterior"), ...)

Arguments

object

An fp_occu object.

nsim

Number of datasets.

seed

Optional integer seed.

truth

Parameter values to simulate from: "mean" (default) uses the posterior means for every dataset; "posterior" uses a different random posterior draw for each dataset, which carries the uncertainty of the fit into the simulations.

...

Unused.

Value

A list of nsim elements, each a list with data (an fp_data object with the structure of the original data) and truth (the generating values on the scale of the output of fp_occu(), the latent states z, the false-positive rate of each site p10_site, and its mean p10_bar).

Details

The recorder effects, when the model has them, are kept at their values in the chosen draw (or their posterior means), so the simulated data have the same recorders with the same effects. Site effects on the false-positive rate (fp_occu(random_fp = TRUE)) are kept at their values in the draw with truth = "posterior"; with truth = "mean", whose site effects would be shrunk towards zero, new ones are drawn from a normal distribution with the posterior mean of sd_fp_site as standard deviation. Under the multiple-methods design, an automated occasion at an occupied site is a detection with probability \(p_{11}\) and at an unoccupied site with probability \(p_{10}\); verified occasions are detections with probability \(r_{11}\) at occupied sites only. Under the observation-confirmation design, true and false observations are drawn independently, as in simulate_fp().

See also

fp_calibrate_fit(), simulate_fp()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 200, nocc = 10, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ 1, random_recorder = FALSE)
new <- simulate(m, nsim = 2, seed = 1)
new[[1]]$data
new[[1]]$truth$p10_bar
} # }
